text: Godrick the Grafted retreated to Stormveil Castle after inheriting his Great Rune and began grafting the limbs of conquered enemies onto his own body; in the second phase of his boss fight, he grafts a dragon's head onto a severed arm to gain additional power.
The boss fight against Rennala takes place in a dream-like golden night sky space formed from her memories and power.
Malenia's second phase causes scarlet rot to bloom into flower-like growths around her as she stops containing the god within her.

Dragonlord Placidusax is the oldest boss in the game, a multi-headed ancient dragon who once served as an Elden Lord of a previous age under a god that vanished when the Greater Will arrived; he is found in a pocket of stopped time within crumbling Farum Azula, a realm of ruins floating in an eternal storm outside the flow of time, waiting eternally for a god that will never return.
Lansseax was worshipped by the Gelmir Cavalry, a warrior culture that maintained the old Draconic faith against the Golden Order.

Fortissax was the dragon companion of Godwyn the Golden; after Godwyn was murdered on the Night of the Black Knives, Fortissax descended into the Erdtree's roots to fight the spreading Deathblight and protect Godwyn's remains, remaining loyal to him even through his transformation into the Prince of Death — an unwinnable battle it still fights eternally, never having won.
Fortissax attacks with golden lightning associated with Godwyn, reflecting his grief and vigil over his lost companion.
The Ancestor Spirits are spiritual representatives of the Crucible Age, a time before the Erdtree when species boundaries were fluid.
The Regal Ancestor Spirit is found in Nokron, the underground Eternal City of the Nox people, who were cast below ground by the Greater Will for trying to create their own Elden Ring.
The Fire Giant is the last survivor of the giants, a people who worshipped the Fell God and were destroyed in a war waged by Marika due to their flame challenging the Erdtree's dominance.
The Fire Giant had his legs severed and was chained to the Forge of the Giants, forced to maintain the flame of his destroyed people's faith.
In the Fire Giant's second phase, he tears off his own leg to expose the flame within his body.
The Elden Beast is described as the living physical form of the Golden Order itself, functioning as a law rather than a conscious monster.
When Godfrey returns during the Shattering, he first appears as a ghost challenging the player in Leyndell, then later as his full human self after the Erdtree's thorns fall.

Godfrey's second phase reveals Hoarah Loux, the berserker name and identity he held before Marika elevated him into the Elden Lord; near the end of the fight he tears the spirit Serosh from his shoulders, killing his restrainer and becoming his unrestrained primal self again.
The Hoarah Loux phase fights bare-armed with grappling and throwing techniques, reflecting a combat style from before civilization formalized it.
Radagon, fought as the second-to-last boss of the main game, is revealed to be the same divine being as Marika, sharing one divine body.
Radagon fights using holy power drawn from the Golden Order's fundamental energies.
The red-gold nails embedded in Radagon's body are self-inflicted, representing his attempt to fuse himself with the Elden Ring through divine will, which ultimately failed.

After Radagon falls in battle, he transforms into Marika and then into the Elden Beast, which emerges from his body; the Elden Beast was sent to the Lands Between by the Greater Will to carry the Elden Ring and is the living embodiment of its Order.
Astel, Naturalborn of the Void, is an alien being that arrived in the Lands Between inside a meteor and did not originate from the world's own cosmology.
Two versions of Astel appear in the game: one in the Lake of Rot and one at the end of Ranni's questline.
Astel's body resembles a star-formed crustacean with a vast insectoid face, operating on alien logic unrelated to the Golden Order or Crucible.

The Frenzied Flame Proscriber, also called the Three Fingers Servant, is represented in-game by frenzied flame enemies and the Three Fingers in Leyndell's undercity rather than as a single named boss.
Crucible Knight Siluria is found in the Deeproot Depths and is among the most ancient Crucible Knights, guarding a space tied to the oldest history of the Lands Between.

Ulcerated Tree Spirits are the transformed bodies of beings who offered themselves to the Erdtree's grace but were rejected, yet still had grace energy flow through them, creating animated corruption.
The glintstone dragons Smarag and Adula are ancient dragons whose bodies have become partially crystalline through long exposure to glintstone, letting them channel starlight through their breath.
Royal Knight Loretta is found guarding the entrance to the Haligtree in the Consecrated Snowfield, and also appears as a summonable spirit ash.
The Tibia Mariner is a skeletal boatman found across the Lands Between who commands undead armies and summons an ancient dragon turtle in some fights.
The Tibia Mariner represents a boatman tasked with ferrying souls to the afterlife, still attempting this duty in a world where Marika's removal of the Rune of Death made death inconsistent.
The Grafted Scion, fought at the start of the game, is a creature made entirely of assembled arms and weapons with no original body remaining, reflecting Godrick's grafting philosophy.
The Fell Twins are enormous Omen bosses found in optional underground areas, representing Omens who grew unmanaged and unprotected unlike demigod Omens such as Morgott and Mohg.

Mohg, Lord of Blood, built Mohgwyn Palace around a wound in the world tied to the Formless Mother, using her gifts to build a blood dynasty and declaring himself Lord of Blood; he kidnapped Miquella to use him as a vehicle for his own ascension.

Margit, the Fell Omen, is Morgott, the Omen King, in disguise; Morgott took his lineage's Great Rune to Leyndell and placed himself on the Elden Throne as a guardian rather than Elden Lord, disguising himself as the merchant and prophet Margit to warn tarnished away from the capital and test their worthiness before revealing his true identity as guardian of the throne.
Romina, Saint of the Bud, is a being of scarlet rot connected to the Land of Shadow's history and the rot's ongoing presence in the world.
Bayle the Dread is the most powerful ancient dragon encountered outside Farum Azula, pursued by veteran dragon slayer Eygon for vengeance.
Midra, Lord of Frenzied Flame, was a nobleman who came to the Land of Shadow seeking something and instead encountered the Three Fingers, leading to his dissolution into the Frenzied Flame.

The Scadutree Avatar is the Great Guardian of the Scadutree, a shadow tree counterpart to the Erdtree that grows in the Land of Shadow in a realm alongside, not within, the Golden Order's world, connected to Marika's hidden origins.

Commander Gaius is a boar-riding general in the Land of Shadow fully devoted to military service under Messmer's campaign, riding an enormous armored boar through the Scadutree region and fighting with tactical precision, identifying the player simply as a problem within his patrol duties.
The Red Wolf of Radagon guards the Debate Parlor in the Academy of Raya Lucaria and fights using Radagon's own sorcerous techniques.
Godskin Noble and Godskin Apostle belong to a religious order dedicated to slaying gods and wearing their skin, with its founding and theology left unexplained by the game.
In Rennala's boss fight, the first phase requires breaking the students carrying her protective golden light, while the second phase has her summon creatures reborn through her Great Rune of rebirth.
Rennala's second-phase summons include a reborn Glintstone Dragon and a troll, among other legendary creatures given new forms through her rebirth power.
Erdtree Avatars found at minor Erdtrees grow directly out of the trees themselves, acting as the Erdtree's own ambulatory immune response.
Valiant Gargoyles are stone constructs animated by Golden Order power that guard the coffin leading to the Deeproot Depths and Godwyn's resting place.
The Mimic Tear is a silver tear of living mercury native to the eternal cities of the Nox, encountered in Nokron, that copies the player's exact appearance, weapons, and spells.
Rykard's serpent god boss form represents the complete expression of what Rykard became after fully merging with the serpent he devoured, rather than wearing a human face.
A human voice speaks through Rykard's serpent form, indicating that a vestige of Rykard's own consciousness persists and still chooses to act even from within the god-devouring serpent's body.
The Night's Cavalry Leader is the most powerful of the Night's Cavalry, a group encountered only after dark at specific locations.
Demi-Human Queen Gilika and her variants lead groups of Demi-Human enemies and represent one of many peoples of the Lands Between who exist outside the Golden Order's framework of value.
Malenia, the Blighted Bloom and her variants are beings of scarlet rot that have taken a plant-like, flower form, combining biological lushness with cosmic corruption.

Divine Beast Dancing Lion is a sacred construct rather than a natural animal, built to embody wild divine power using storm, snow, and thunder, reflecting the Land of Shadow's more reciprocal relationship with nature compared to the Golden Order.
Messmer, Mother of Fingers is revealed to be the original source of all Two Fingers and Three Fingers found throughout the Lands Between.
Messmer, Mother of Fingers is found broken in the Land of Shadow, her connection to the Greater Will severed or compromised.
Relena, Twin Moon Knight is found in Castle Ensis and wields both golden and cold moon magic, representing a tradition of moon sorcery that parallels Rennala's in a different context.
Putrescent Knight guards the Cerulean Coast, defending a space of beauty that is already affected by rot and dissolution.
The Putrescent Knight's armor is encrusted with evidence of decay, showing it is partly consumed by the same dissolution process it was appointed to guard against, yet it continues its duty.
Romina, Saint of the Bud embodies rot as a form of growth and renewal rather than simple decay, with her arena filling with rot blooms as the fight progresses.
Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy, took his Great Rune to Volcano Manor and merged with a great serpent, becoming a god-devouring blasphemy.
Radahn, the Starscourge, claimed his Great Rune and continued holding the stars in place using gravity magic.
When fought in the ruined desert north of Redmane Castle, Radahn still rides Leonard even while feral and consumed by rot.
Leonard stays beside Radahn's body after his death.
Radahn survived the battle but the scarlet rot consumed his mind, reducing him to a feral, mindless creature that ate corpses.
Malenia wakes only when the tarnished disturbs her after navigating the Consecrated Snowfield and the corrupted Haligtree.
Upon waking, Malenia says: "I dreamt for so long. My flesh was dull gold and my blood was rot," and "I await him still," referring to Miquella.
Malenia introduces herself as Malenia, Blade of Miquella, and declares she has never known defeat.
Inside the Erdtree, the Tarnished confronts Radagon, described as Marika's other, devoted half who tried to repair what Marika broke.
The Elden Beast is fought as a creature of golden starlight within a void of absolute darkness.
Because the death curse mark was split, Godwyn's soul died but his body remained alive, corrupting and spreading underground as a growth known as the Prince of Death.
